findings.title: parseQuantity accepts invalid input and silently produces NaN, corrupting cart totals
findings.problem: parseQuantity(text) calls parseInt(text) with no radix argument and no validation of the result. Non-numeric or malformed input (e.g. empty string, whitespace, non-digit text) yields NaN, and even partially-numeric input like '08x' is parsed leniently without any error signaled to the caller.
findings.recommendedFix: Use parseInt(text, 10), validate the result with Number.isInteger and reject/throw or clamp to a safe default (e.g. 0 or 1) when NaN or negative; consider also rejecting non-integer or negative quantities explicitly.

findings.title: applyDiscount does not validate or clamp the percent argument
findings.problem: The doc comment states percent should be 0-100, but applyDiscount performs no validation or clamping of the percent parameter before using it in the calculation.
findings.recommendedFix: Clamp percent to the documented [0, 100] range (or throw a validation error) at the top of applyDiscount before performing the calculation.

findings.title: No test coverage for session.js or applyDiscount/parseQuantity in cart.js
findings.problem: The only test file present exercises solely the subtotal() function. applyDiscount and parseQuantity in src/cart.js, and all exports of src/session.js (createSession, isExpired, refresh, including the session-expiry boundary condition), have zero test coverage.
findings.recommendedFix: Add unit tests for applyDiscount (including boundary/out-of-range percent), parseQuantity (including invalid input), and session.js (createSession, isExpired at exact expiresAt boundary, and refresh including its throw-on-expired path).

findings.title: Sessions remain valid at their expiry instant
findings.problem: The comment specifies that a session is valid strictly before its expiry instant, but isExpired uses a strict greater-than comparison. At exactly session.expiresAt, the session is treated as not expired.
findings.recommendedFix: Use now >= session.expiresAt, then add boundary tests for times immediately before, exactly at, and immediately after expiry.

findings.title: Discount percentage bounds are not enforced
findings.problem: The function documents percent as being in the range 0-100 but performs no validation. Negative percentages increase the total, and percentages above 100 produce negative totals.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate that percent is finite and within 0-100 before calculating, and reject invalid values explicitly.

findings.title: Quantity parsing accepts malformed customer input
findings.problem: parseInt accepts numeric prefixes and returns NaN for some invalid inputs. The function does not enforce a complete, finite, positive integer quantity.
findings.recommendedFix: Parse with an explicit radix and validate the complete input as a finite positive integer, rejecting malformed values rather than coercing them.

findings.title: Off-by-one boundary check in session expiration
findings.problem: The docstring states that a session is valid strictly before its expiry instant (`valid strictly before its expiry instant`), which means it is expired at `now >= session.expiresAt`. However, `isExpired` evaluates `now > session.expiresAt`, considering the session valid at the exact expiration timestamp `now === session.expiresAt`.
findings.recommendedFix: Update `isExpired` to return `now >= session.expiresAt;` to align implementation with the documented contract.

findings.title: Missing radix parameter in parseInt for quantity parsing
findings.problem: Calling `parseInt(text)` without specifying a radix defaults to decimal in modern ECMAScript for numeric strings without prefixes, but does not guard against invalid non-numeric characters, negative numbers, floats, or unexpected strings (such as leading zeros or whitespace), and returns `NaN` or truncated integers without validation.
findings.recommendedFix: Specify radix 10 (`parseInt(text, 10)`) and validate that the result is an integer greater than zero.
